persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent's day centers on Anthropic's IPO filing: he says losses were below expectations, growth was in line and customer mix was strong, which lifted all AI stocks. **SMH** rose 2.74%, **AMD** 2.80% and **Nvidia** 2.39%, while **Meta** was negative because of its roughly $95 billion new share sale plan. **Broadcom** is seeking $63 billion of financing, so he thinks financing fears are not over.

In Brazil, Lula's election win sent **EWZ** down 19.82%, **MercadoLibre** down 7.81% and **Nubank** down 16.95%; Bora says he likes both companies. Oil is still above $100, the Fed decision arrives at 21:00 Turkey time and the odds of a December hike are high. He also said he will be quiet today and until tomorrow evening.

items.title: Anthropic Saved the Nasdaq
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing came in better than expected: losses below expectations, growth in line and a strong customer mix. According to Bora Özkent, the first-half operating loss is $693 million and the ~$8.9 billion spent on compute equals 55% of revenue. The company holds roughly $140 billion in cash and is expected to raise another $100 billion in the IPO; the $1.52 trillion valuation is debatable because of off-balance-sheet commitments with companies like Amazon and Broadcom. The news lifted SMH 2.74%, AMD 2.80% and Nvidia 2.39%; Meta was negative because of its $95 billion share sale plan, and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom said they may take up to $5 billion of shares in total. Broadcom is seeking $63 billion of financing, while SpaceX closed $40 billion with Apollo. After Lula's win in Brazil, EWZ fell 19.82%, MercadoLibre 7.81% and Nubank 16.95%, and Bora says he likes both companies. Oil is above $100; the report that Iran may agree to send enriched uranium to Russia awaits confirmation. The Fed decision comes at 21:00 Turkey time; no hike is expected but the odds for December are high.

persons.name: jrouldz
persons.digest: jrouldz is rebalancing after earnings: he was ready to sell **SoFi** on a bad report but keeps holding after the strong results. He is ready to sell **Visa** after a 150% gain over 6 years and is close to trimming **Apple** at ~16% of his portfolio. He sees **Amazon** as the market's "safest bet", holds **Robinhood** reluctantly and is glad he avoided **Innodata**.

items.title: Keeping SoFi
items.summary: He was ready to dump SoFi this morning on a bad report, but the company delivered so he keeps holding; he is working to reduce total fintech exposure.

items.title: Visa sale
items.summary: He is ready to sell his Visa position after earnings: it returned 150% in 6 years and at ~30x earnings and a $750B market cap the best case is another 2x in a few years.

assets.note: Ready to sell; sees more attractive opportunities.

items.title: Apple trim
items.summary: Apple has grown to ~16% of his portfolio so he is close to trimming but would never sell it all.

items.title: Amazon the safest bet
items.summary: He calls Amazon the "safest bet" on the market and would pick it if he could own one stock; Meta carries more risk but more upside.

assets.note: Safest bet; high upside, limited downside.

items.title: Reluctantly holding Robinhood
items.summary: He is jaded by the fintech sector, is exploring next-gen alternatives, but reluctantly holds HOOD.

items.title: Innodata drop
items.summary: He wrote that Innodata's 550 layoffs highlight customer-concentration risk, the chart looks poor and he will watch the Nov 5 earnings.

assets.note: Customer concentration risk; glad to have avoided it.

persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest: cevikfinance reads **SoFi**'s pledge to stop diluting shares as good news for investors and calls the results "terrific". He listed six companies that beat on earnings and guidance since yesterday: **SOFI**, **CLS**, **CDNS**, **AGYS**, **UPS**, **CNC**. On Chinese clouds' memory contract requests running to 2035 he added a note that memory stocks are cyclical.

items.title: SoFi won't dilute
items.summary: He read SoFi's statement that it won't dilute further as good news for investors.

assets.note: No dilution; good news for investors.

items.title: Six companies beating estimates
items.summary: Companies that beat on both profit and revenue and guided well since yesterday: SOFI, CLS, CDNS, AGYS, UPS, CNC; KO, ITRI, HCA and GLW guided close to estimates.

items.title: Short company news
items.summary: He summarized company news such as Microsoft's voluntary departure offer to 60,000 employees, Apple's M6 MacBook Pro and TSMC considering CoWoS price hikes.

assets.note: Launched the M6 MacBook Pro; kept prices despite memory costs.

items.title: Warsh and Fed expectations
items.summary: He relayed that some analysts think Warsh may sound less hawkish than expected because credit markets have shut, and asked for views.

items.title: Chinese clouds and the memory cycle
items.summary: On Chinese clouds seeking memory contracts through 2035, he noted that memory stocks are cyclical and Chinese makers could overproduce.

assets.note: Long-term demand is positive but memory stocks are cyclical.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies

mentions.quote: So if rates fall, it will rocket to the 40-45 band.
I was mentally prepared to dump $SOFI this morning on a bad report and then they ended up delivering so I am going to keep holding
$SOFI says we won't dilute any more, we don't need to. Good news for investors.
$SOFI +11% Following a Q3 earnings beat, raised 2026 guidance, and a 2027 outlook above Wall Street estimates.

holdings.why: ulkser says the stock could reach a 40-45 band if rates fall and cevikfinance welcomes the end of dilution, but nobody gave a clear add level.
holdings.opinion: The earnings and the no-new-capital message are positive, but at 18.8% this is the portfolio's biggest single-stock risk, and an 11% jump may have enlarged it further. Rate direction and credit quality are what to watch.
ai_points: For: guidance was raised and the 2027 revenue guide beat estimates.
For: management said no capital raise is needed.
Against: the 18.8% weight creates single-stock concentration risk.
Against: ulkser's 40-45 scenario depends on rates falling.

holdings.opinion: The sources have no concrete data on Turkish assets today; at 12.9% the weight is high and carries currency and rate risk. Global risk appetite and lira developments are worth watching.
ai_points: For: global risk appetite is positive today.
Against: no concrete Turkey-specific rationale in today's sources.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: D.A. Davidson upgraded Broadcom $AVGO to Buy from Neutral, raising its price target to $400 from $350.
Broadcom is seeking $63 billion of financing.

holdings.why: wallstengine relayed D.A. Davidson's upgrade with a $400 target and the $63B Anthropic financing, but made no buy or sell call of its own.
holdings.opinion: The Anthropic financing makes 2027 deliveries visible and, at 12.9%, Broadcom is the core of the portfolio's AI chip exposure. The key risk is that the financing depends on a debt structure and on Anthropic's IPO going ahead.
ai_points: For: the $63B financing supports 2027 deliveries.
For: D.A. Davidson raised its target to $400, seeing 16x 2027 EPS.
Against: banks had considered pulling out over AI debt and interest-rate concerns.

holdings.name: Meta Platforms A

mentions.quote: The reason Meta is negative is that it is looking for money.
$META's $25B stock sale draws 5x demand. The offering was priced at $625 per share.
Others like $META definitely carry more risk but probably more upside potential to match.

holdings.why: Bora Özkent sees the stock as negative because of its funding search, while wallstengine reported the $625 sale drew 5x demand.
holdings.opinion: The share sale dilutes, but 5x demand and Nvidia/AMD participation are signs of confidence. At 12.8%, the return on AI spending and the planned $60B sale program for 2027 are the main risks.
ai_points: For: the sale drew 5x demand, with over half going to long-only investors.
Against: per Bora Özkent, the funding search weighs on the stock.
Against: total offerings rose to $37.5B with a new program planned for 2027.

holdings.name: BWX Technologies

mentions.quote: BWX Technologies and Antares Sign a TRISO Nuclear Fuel Supply Agreement

holdings.why: WallStDiaries relayed the multi-year TRISO fuel framework with Antares, but gave no valuation view.
holdings.opinion: The deal is small (initially 1 MTU) but a positive signal for micro-reactor demand. At 10.5% the stock is tied to the nuclear and data-center power theme; new order flow is what to watch.
ai_points: For: the multi-year fuel supply deal signals demand.
Against: the deal is initially small in volume.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: Ahead of the decision, the US 10-year yield fell to 4.97%, below the critical 5% threshold.

holdings.why: WallStDiaries reported the 10-year yield dropping below 5% but gave no buy or sell case for the fund.
holdings.opinion: A long-duration bond fund is highly sensitive to the rate decision and Warsh's tone; if December hike odds stay high, yields could rise again and weigh on the fund. At 8% it balances an equity-heavy portfolio, but no data today sets direction.
ai_points: For: the 10-year yield slipped below the 5% threshold.
Against: per Bora Özkent, the odds of a December hike are high.
Against: the Fed decision is today and long bonds are sensitive to its tone.
